title: Certificates of Deposit: Bump-Up Rate Increases
content:
Among Piedmont Crescent Bank's Certificates of Deposit, a bump-up certificate lets its owner move the certificate onto a better published rate partway through a term. This page sets out when Piedmont Crescent Bank accepts such a request and what the new rate is.

## When a bump-up is accepted

On a tier that allows bump-ups, the owner may ask to raise the rate once per term. The request is accepted only if every one of these holds on the bank's record:

- the certificate is active;
- no bump-up has yet been used in the current term;
- the tier's standard APY as published today is higher than the certificate's APY less the bonus points already built into this term's rate;
- the request falls inside the tier's bump-up window.

If any of them fails, the request is declined and the certificate is left exactly as it was.

## The bump-up window

The window is counted in calendar months from the start date of the current term. A request is accepted up to and including the date that lies the window's number of months after the term start date; where that month has no day with the same number, the last day of that month is used instead.

## Tier settings

| Tier | Bump-ups allowed per term | Bump-up window (calendar months from term start) |
|---|---|---|
| 6-Month Certificate | 0 | not applicable |
| 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate | 0 | not applicable |
| 12-Month Certificate | 0 | not applicable |
| 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate | 1 | 15 |
| 36-Month Certificate | 0 | not applicable |
| 60-Month Certificate | 0 | not applicable |

## The new rate

After a bump-up, the certificate carries today's published standard interest rate for its tier with the term's existing bonus points on top, and today's published standard APY with those points on top. Both take effect from the date of the request. Interest for days before that date stays as it was.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates, 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate)

| Term start date | Request date | Inside the window? |
|---|---|---|
| 31 January 2025 | 30 April 2026 | Yes; April has no 31st, so the window closes on 30 April 2026 |
| 31 January 2025 | 1 May 2026 | No |
| 10 March 2025 | 10 June 2026 | Yes, the last day |

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

A certificate shows an APY of 4.05 percent, of which 0.15 points are a bonus earned at the term's start, so its unbonused APY is 3.90 percent. If the tier's published standard APY today is 4.10 percent, that is higher than 3.90, and a first request in the window is accepted: the new APY is 4.10 plus 0.15, that is 4.25 percent, and the new rate is today's published standard rate plus the same 0.15 points. Had the published APY been 3.90 percent, it would not be higher, and the request would be declined.
